text:
sre-incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming gateway p99 latency spike detected for /v1/stream (hosted). p95 breached for the last 5m. Auto-escalation to on-call. Incident INC-5792 created. :rotating_light:

maria: seeing p99 ~ 4.2s on gateway, p95 ~ 1.1s. Tail looks like chunking stalls — clients hang waiting for the next SSE chunk.

anil: confirming, traces show long kernel write waits from envoy->upstream for chunk flush. upstream time looks fine. suspect buffering at gateway/proxy layer or client backpressure.

devon: any config changes rolled in last hour? I see a deploy for gateway mux at 1789121000 but rollout finished.

jordan: rolling windows: spike coincides with a surge from a single customer (ingest-subscriber-79). They opened a long-lived SSE connection and started polling events aggressively.

maria: customer traffic pattern could cause head-of-line blocking in our connection mux. For immediate mitigation: 1) enable per-connection throttling for long-lived streams 2) force flush frequency lower bound on gateway (disable coalescing) 3) add temporary routing to alternate gateway pool.

anil: ops commands I'm running now:
```bash
# reroute traffic away from gateway-a to gateway-b
rbctl route add --from host/gateway-a --to host/gateway-b --match "/v1/stream" --weight 0.0
# increase flush interval to avoid coalescing (fallback throttle)
kubectl -n infra patch configgateway gateway-config --type merge -p '{"spec":{"flush_ms":20}}'
```

oncall-bot: action taken: traffic partially rerouted; gateway-a weight set to 0 for /v1/stream.

devon: after reroute p95 dropped to 0.9s, p99 down to 1.3s. Good improvement but still above SLO for a subset.

maria: capturing a heap of envoy stats and tcp socket states from gateway-a for further analysis. Key flags: envoy version=1.25.0, conn_retries small, upstream_busy high.

jordan: customer impact: several clients reported stalled streams and UI hangs. PM-olivia, please confirm customer-facing comms.

pm-olivia: drafting status update to customer and incident page. Will note mitigation and ongoing investigation.

anil: logs snippet from gateway-a:
```
[2026-03-14T18:10:12Z] warn upstream_write_timeout: id=0x7f3a, queue_len=342, socket_write_wait_ms=1200
[2026-03-14T18:10:13Z] info conn_state: remote=10.2.3.48:56322 rx_buf=65536 tx_buf=0 backlog=128
```

maria: looks like sokcet tx buffer starved — outbound chunks aren't making it to client because upstream is writing faster than lower-layer can flush. Could be TCP window/clamping with our proxy's coalescing.

devon: quick test: reduce chunk size at runtime for model responses (prefer more frequent smaller chunks). Pushing a small middleware patch to truncate chunk sizes for /v1/stream to 512 bytes.

anil: patch deployed to canary. Observing decreased write_wait and lower backlog on canary nodes.

maria: running full handoff to next on-call @anil in 10m. Logging all actions in INC-5792.

jordan: started collecting client-side timings from telemetry: many clients show large read stalls (socket read paused for ~1.5s). Points to proxy/coalescing + client backpressure interplay.

pm-olivia: customer comms sent: "We observed streaming delays for a small subset of users due to a traffic pattern causing temporary buffering at the streaming gateway. We’ve rerouted traffic and applied mitigations; we continue to investigate root cause and will follow up."

maria: next steps for postmortem: 1) root cause — interaction between connection mux coalescing and large-volume long-lived clients 2) propose safety defaults: per-connection chunk flush timeout, per-customer stream rate caps 3) add synthetic canaries that simulate long-lived SSE clients to catch regression.

anil: follow-up immediate action item tracker: [ ] revert coalescing default to conservative (done), [ ] implement per-connection throttles (in progress), [ ] instrumentation for socket-level backlog (open).

devon: leaving notes for oncall-handoff: if p99 > 2s again, escalate to eng-runtime and consider temporarily rejecting new long-lived streams from offending customer via ACL.

maria: patch to middleware chunk size landed and rolled to 20% -> 100% over 12m. Observed stable p95/p99 now: p95 0.65s, p99 0.95s. Marking customer-impact as resolved for now, keeping INC-5792 open for RCA. :white_check_mark:

jordan: adding correlation graphs to the incident page: gateway flush_ms vs p99; customer-subscriber id.

pm-olivia: scheduling follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 9:30am PT.

oncall-bot: Handoff: maria -> anil. oncall schedule: anil is now on-call for incidents INC-5792. :wave:
